Survey-design models in table_regression()

Source: R/table_regression_survey.R
table_regression_survey.Rd

table_regression() reads the fits of a survey::svydesign() or survey::as.svrepdesign() design: survey::svyglm() (and its replicate sibling svrepglm), survey::svyolr(), and survey::svycoxph() (and svrepcoxph). They are read as design-based throughout: the coefficients, the variance and the reference distribution all come from survey. The note names the design, the number of primary sampling units and the residual degrees of freedom.

Usage

table_regression(
  models,
  vcov = "classical",
  nested = FALSE,
  show_fit_stats = NULL,
  ...  # the arguments of every class: see ?table_regression
)

This family has no argument of its own. The other arguments are documented in table_regression(); the values they take for survey-design models are listed below.

Engines

ClassEngineAMEExponentiateBlocksvcov
svyglmsurvey::svyglm()yes (design-based)OR / IRR-classical (design-based)
svyolrsurvey::svyolr()per category (design-based)OR (logit)Thresholdsclassical (design-based)
svycoxphsurvey::svycoxph()noHR-classical (design-based)

AME: whether the average-marginal-effects columns are available. Exponentiate: what exponentiate = TRUE gives. Blocks: the labeled blocks of rows the class adds below its coefficients. vcov: the values of vcov the class accepts. The same rows are returned by subset(table_regression_models(), family == "Survey-weighted").

What the table shows

Coefficient rows. One row per coefficient, as for the matching model without a design: svyglm as glm, svyolr as MASS::polr() (with its Thresholds block, table_regression_ordinal), svycoxph as survival::coxph() (table_regression_survival).

AME. The Horvitz-Thompson estimator: the mean unit-level effect weighted by the sampling weights of the analytic sample, with its variance from the delta method on the design vcov. It is tested on the same distribution as the coefficient rows. svyolr gives one effect per category.

Counts. Both are reported: the observed n and the Weighted n the estimates describe. svycoxph adds the number of events.

Values of the shared arguments

vcov, cluster

"classical" only, which here is the design-based variance of the fit (Taylor linearization or replicates). Clustering belongs in the design, survey::svydesign(ids = ~cluster, ...), not in the table call.

nested

FALSE only. See What is refused, and why.

show_fit_stats

By default n and Weighted n, with AIC for svyglm and the number of events for svycoxph. On request, "eff_p" and "concordance"; see Fit statistics.

exponentiate

Odds or rate ratios for svyglm under the logit or log link, odds ratios for svyolr (logit), hazard ratios for svycoxph.

standardized

Refused.

Standard errors, degrees of freedom and intervals

Inference is Wald t at the degrees of freedom survey writes on the fit: df.residual for svyglm and svyolr, degf.resid or degf.residual for the two Cox engines. This is what survey::regTermTest() takes as its denominator. It is not survey::degf(design), and it is not re-derived here: the engines of survey do not share one expression (a Cox fit carries degf(design) - p + 1 although it has no intercept for the + 1 to cancel, so it ends one above the two other classes). The value is read off the object, and the note prints it. The interval uses the same distribution, and so do the average marginal effects.

Fit statistics

  • "aic": svyglm keeps an AIC row. survey's extractAIC.svyglm computes the design-based AIC of Lumley & Scott (2015).

  • "eff_p": the effective number of parameters of the design, the first element of survey's extractAIC (the sum of the Rao-Scott eigenvalues), reported beside the AIC on request.

  • "concordance": the concordance of a svycoxph fit goes to the note, or to a row on request.

What is refused, and why

  • Every model-derived variance (HC*, CR*, "bootstrap", "jackknife"). The design is the variance authority: the fit's Taylor or replicate variance is already the robust variance for the declared design. The way to change the estimator is to change the design.

  • "bic", "aicc", "deviance", "log_lik", the pseudo-R-squared tokens ("pseudo_r2_mcfadden", "pseudo_r2_nagelkerke", "pseudo_r2_tjur") and "r2_deviance" for a table of design fits, and "aic" when no model of the table is a svyglm. A design-based fit is estimated without a likelihood, and survey's own deviance() returns a sign-flipped likelihood-ratio statistic on one Cox engine and a bare zero on the other. BIC.svyglm requires a maximal model and has no default.

  • nested = TRUE. There is no likelihood to compare, so every change statistic would be empty, and a block of empty rows reads like an answer. Put the models side by side with nested = FALSE, and test a term under the design with survey::regTermTest().

  • The AME for svycoxph, on the same ground as for a Cox model without a design (table_regression_survival).

  • The "rmst" and "risk_diff" columns for svycoxph: their uncertainty comes from resampling subjects, which ignores the strata and clusters the design declares. Use survey::svykm() for a marginal curve.

  • standardized.

See also

table_regression() for the arguments shared by all classes; table_regression_models() for the registry of supported classes and the other families; table_categorical_svy() and table_continuous_svy() for descriptive tables of a design; the Summary tables from a survey design article.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("survey", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("api", package = "survey")
  des <- survey::svydesign(ids = ~dnum, weights = ~pw, data = apiclus1,
                           fpc = ~fpc)
  fit <- survey::svyglm(api00 ~ ell + meals, design = des)
  print(table_regression(fit))
}
